title: Coroner's jury says Fort Smith elder died of natural causes
subtitle: Jury recommends developing procedures to deal with dangerous levels of intoxication
article: A coroner's jury has ruled that a 66-year-old Fort Smith man died of natural causes after being found unresponsive in RCMP cells.
Police arrested Wilfred Emile for public intoxication on Oct. 16 last year.

He lost consciousness in his jail cell shortly after. Emile was taken by ambulance to the Fort Smith health centre where, according to the coroner's jury, "he received significant medical intervention."
The next morning, Emile was medevaced to the Royal Alexandra Hospital in Edmonton, where he received treatment for three days until being moved back to Fort Smith.
Emile was then moved back to the Fort Smith health centre, but by then it was to clear he was not going to recover. He was there to be with his family in his final days.
According to the jury's report, he passed away on Oct. 26 with family at his side.

Though the jury found Emile died of natural causes, it recommended that the RCMP and health department develop a procedure for dealing with people who seem to have dangerous levels of intoxication. It recommended that procedure be communicated to police officers and health workers, as well as housing and public welfare workers.
An earlier investigation by the Medicine Hat Police Force found no indication that RCMP used force against Emile. It found his death was strictly a medical issue.
